base_member_text: [L43,L55] (MED/integer-overflow) An accepted interval count near INT_MAX can overflow the signed loop index on its final increment, causing undefined behavior.
audit_member_text: [L55] (MED/integer-overflow) For interval counts near INT_MAX, the final i += numprocs can overflow signed int before the loop condition is rechecked.

adversarial.rationale: The scanf check handles failed conversion but accepts a representable INT_MAX, and the only numerical exit check is n==0. With one process, the last iteration at i=INT_MAX executes i+=1 before retesting, overflowing signed int; no wider loop-index declaration or cap exists.

base_member_text: [L50-L59] (LOW/input-validation) Negative interval counts enter the calculation branch and report zero as the approximation instead of rejecting the input.
audit_member_text: [L50-L59] (LOW/input-validation) Negative interval counts pass the zero-only exit check and produce an empty integral reported as a pi approximation.

adversarial.rationale: A successfully scanned negative n is broadcast and enters the else branch because the guard tests equality with zero only. Every rank starts with a positive i, skips the integration loop and reduces a signed-zero partial sum, which root prints as its pi approximation.
